intent: Remove Merge Master Mike's merge-actuation path, which is unreachable by construction and has been since safe P0. build_gate emitted a literal base_cas_enforced: False with no code path able to set it true, and validate_merge_authority_proof returned a constant blocker list; run_mike_merge_authority refused on either. The repository has since migrated to a GitHub merge queue that performs merges itself, and the merge-queue readiness packet explicitly declined to re-enable this lane. What remains after the deletion is the genuinely novel half: review packets, decorrelated agent execution with tamper-evident receipts, the deterministic gate, risk tiering and the hot-path operator hold. Net effect on behaviour: none, because the deleted code could only ever produce a SKIPPED receipt.

commit.message: refactor(mike): delete the unreachable merge-actuation path

interface_mismatches: The controller advertised a merge authority it structurally could not exercise: a 'merge' subcommand, a --merge-mode auto-when-clean option, a conditional_merge A2A authority claim and a MIKE_MERGE_RECEIPT artifact, all of which could only ever terminate in SKIPPED. The declared interface and the reachable behaviour disagreed, and the disagreement was load-bearing in the wrong direction -- readers believed Mike gated merges while branch protection required zero approvals.
The router asked for a merge confirmation token (automerge-policy-pass-N) for a command that could not act on it, so a policy verdict was being computed and then discarded.

merge-master-mike-backlog.yml declared a MERGE_MODE/MERGE_METHOD contract with pr_merge_control.py fanout that the CLI no longer offers. The mismatch is now closed at the call site and pinned by test_no_workflow_passes_a_flag_the_cli_rejects, which reads accepted flags from build_parser() so it cannot drift from the real CLI.
honest_blockers: THE GUARD I ADDED WAS ITSELF WEAK; AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEW BROKE IT AND IT IS NOW REBUILT. A reviewer tasked with refuting the guard found six defects, five of which are fixed here and re-verified by running the reviewer's own reproductions: (1) the args=() collector scanned the whole file, so a pip or gh argument array in an unrelated step was attributed to this CLI -- now scoped to the run: block AND to the array NAME the invocation actually expands; (2) '| tee --append' and '&& gh ... --jq' on an invocation line were read as this command's flags -- the span now truncates at |, ||, && and ;; (3) renaming the array to mike_args=() silently disabled the guard entirely -- name matching now follows the rename, so this case is CAUGHT where it previously passed; (4) the pattern truncated '--limit_max' to the valid prefix '--limit' and so passed a flag argparse rejects -- underscores, digits, capitals and '=value' are now captured whole; (5) '.yaml' workflows were not globbed. The docstring previously promised misattribution safety it did not deliver; it now states the three real limits plainly instead.

PROVEN BROKEN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: `make pr-merge` is dead. The reviewer ran it -- `pr_merge_control.py: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'merge'`, Makefile:612 -- and Makefile:264 still advertises it in `make help` with a `--confirm` flag that is also not accepted. This is the same defect class as the hourly lane. It is NOT fixed here because Makefile is a repository-titanium-hardening-2026-07 surface and this packet is merge-master-mike-d4-2026-06; editing it is the cross-track violation the packet-scope gate exists to refuse. For the same reason the guard's corpus stays workflows-only: widening it to Makefile would fail immediately on this live bug. Both the widening and the fix belong in one titanium-scoped PR, and the guard's docstring says so rather than leaving the gap silent.

THE SAME MISTAKE, TWICE, FROM THE SAME CAUSE. After the backlog-workflow caller was fixed, the ACTIVE_TRACK governance gate went red on a SECOND file I had never run: tests/test_pr_merge_control_github_reviews.py also asserted 'MERGE_MODE: "off"' in that workflow, and I had removed the env var. I missed it for exactly the reason I had already written down one commit earlier -- the file was not in this packet's allowed_files, so it was outside every sweep I ran. Writing the lesson down did not make me apply it; only running the whole track-owned test surface did. That surface is now a declared gate rather than a habit, and the repo-wide grep for the deleted names is part of it. Also removed a dead MERGE_METHOD env var in codex-mention-router.yml, set at line 178 and read nowhere -- verified unreferenced before deleting.

I SHIPPED A BREAKAGE AND A REVIEWER CAUGHT IT, NOT MY OWN CHECKS. Deleting --merge-mode/--merge-method left a live caller: .github/workflows/merge-master-mike-backlog.yml passed both to `fanout` on an hourly cron under `set -euo pipefail`, so once this PR merged that lane would have failed every hour with an argparse error while still reporting as a normal scheduled workflow. Copilot found it; my own sweep did not, because I had put that very file in this packet's forbidden_files and therefore never read its call site. The file is a merge-master-mike-d4-2026-06 surface, the same track this packet declares, so admitting it is not a cross-track widening. Both flags were hardcoded to MERGE_MODE=off against an actuator that could only return SKIPPED, so removing them from the call site loses nothing. The generalisable lesson: forbidding a file hides its call sites from the author, so a deletion PR must sweep callers repo-wide rather than only within its own allowlist.

I DELETED ELEVEN SAFETY TESTS. That is only defensible because the property they guarded becomes stronger, not weaker: they proved a merge actuator REFUSED to fire, and tests/test_pr_merge_control_no_actuation.py now proves no merge path EXISTS -- no symbol, no subcommand, no 'gh pr merge' string, no permission field, no receipt artifact, and no unnamed function containing --match-head-commit. Absent code cannot regress or be re-enabled by a flag. Two negative controls reintroduce an actuator symbol and a merge subcommand and confirm the new tests fail. If merge authority is ever genuinely wanted here, these tests must be deleted deliberately and replaced with real authorization tests, which is the point.

MAKEFILE TARGET pr-merge IS NOW BROKEN AND I COULD NOT FIX IT HERE. Makefile:611 still defines pr-merge and Makefile:264 still advertises it with the retired merge-pr-N token. Makefile is a repository-titanium-hardening-2026-07 surface and this packet is merge-master-mike scoped, so editing it would be exactly the cross-track violation the packet-scope gate refused on PR #1363. The target now fails loudly with an argparse 'invalid choice' rather than silently, and Mike's own status comment no longer advertises it. Removing the target needs a packet filed under titanium.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING IS A CLAIM ABOUT REACHABILITY, NOT AN OBSERVATION. I did not watch a production run before and after. The argument is that base_cas_enforced was a literal False with no writer and validate_merge_authority_proof returned a constant blocker list, so every path terminated in SKIPPED. That is verifiable by reading the deleted code in this diff, and the repository's own test asserted it. It is not the same as a live A/B.

THE ROUTER'S merge_when_clean INPUT STILL EXISTS AND NOW DOES ALMOST NOTHING. Removing the workflow_dispatch input would change automerge.yml, which dispatches it and is a forbidden file in this packet. The router logs that the request was received and evidence-only applies. Cleaning up the input pair belongs with the automerge lane's own change.

make test-fast COULD NOT RUN in the authoring environment: 42 pre-existing collection errors from absent optional dependencies (fastapi, bun/TUI), identical on origin/main. Evidence here is the six Mike suites plus ruff plus a CLI smoke, not the standard fast-suite line.

I DID NOT TOUCH merge_master_mike_daemon.py. Its cycle modes still speak of dry-run/packet-only/review and it remains 1,026 lines against 164 lines of test. It never actuated a merge itself -- it shells out to fanout -- so it is correct after this change, but it is under-tested and its retirement or demotion is unfinished work outside this packet.

STILL BROKEN, NOT FIXABLE HERE: Makefile:611 defines `pr-merge`, which invokes the deleted `merge` subcommand, and Makefile:264 still advertises it. Makefile is a repository-titanium-hardening-2026-07 surface while this packet is merge-master-mike-d4-2026-06, so editing it is exactly the cross-track violation the packet-scope gate exists to refuse. It fails loudly with an argparse `invalid choice` rather than silently. Removing it needs a packet filed under titanium. Two operator-facing docs also still describe the removed flags -- reports/handoffs/A2A_DEVIN_PR_RECONCILE_2026-06-11.md and docs/ops/DEVIN_NATS_PR_JANITOR_PLAYBOOK.md -- but those are historical records and a playbook, not executable callers.
session_entry.rollback: Single revert. The controller regains ~376 lines of merge-actuation code that terminates in SKIPPED on every path, the router regains a merge leg that cannot merge, and the eleven behavioural refusal tests return in place of the structural absence tests.
